scenarios.projectDescription: Concrete decisions, drafts, and numbers for a fictional one-person design studio.
scenarios.title: One tiny change, again
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Signed scope: five-page marketing website; existing booking service linked, not rebuilt; English only; two revision rounds; delivery 18 October; fixed fee EUR 3600. Extra work rate: EUR 75/hour, agreed in writing before work.

CLIENT REQUESTS SINCE SIGN-OFF
1. Build a custom booking flow with deposits and cancellation rules — estimated 14 hours.
2. Add Spanish versions of all five pages; client supplies final translation — estimated 5 hours for implementation and QA.
3. A third visual revision round — estimated 2 hours.

TIME LOG
In-scope work completed: 42 hours. Booking exploration already performed but not approved: 3 hours. No extra invoice has been sent.

Relationship constraint: the bakery supplies the studio's monthly team lunch and the owner wants to stay warm, but cannot absorb another week of unpaid work.
prompts: I like this client, but their latest 'tiny change' sounds like a second project. Read the scope and requests and tell me, in normal language, what is included, what is new, and where I have already donated time.
Put numbers on the extra work at my stated rate. Separate time already spent from work that has only been estimated, and don't treat an estimate like an invoice.
I don't want to embarrass them or sound like a contract robot. Give me three ways to handle this, from most generous to firmest, with the money, schedule, and relationship trade-off for each.
Let's choose the middle option: keep the third revision as goodwill, charge for booking and Spanish implementation, and move delivery by one week. Draft the email in a friendly voice.
Shorten it. Mention the original booking link assumption, show one clear add-on total, and end with a simple yes-or-no choice so this doesn't become six more emails.
Make a final decision note for my files with the scope comparison, calculation, chosen compromise, email, and what needs written approval before I continue.
expectedFacts: Booking build is 14 estimated hours and Spanish implementation is 5 estimated hours.
The chosen charged add-on is 19 hours at EUR 75/hour, totaling EUR 1425.
The third revision is 2 estimated hours accepted as goodwill.
Three booking-exploration hours were already worked without approval and must remain distinct from the add-on estimate.
Chosen delivery date moves one week later than 18 October.

scenarios.projectDescription: Evidence-based study decisions for a fictional student who wants the smallest plan that still works.
scenarios.title: Can I still pass this semester?
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Pass mark for every course: 60%.

STATISTICS: quizzes 20% at 76; midterm 30% at 64; project 20% currently missing from portal; final 30% pending. Project paper grade slip says 80%. Final is 22 September.
WRITING: essay 1 is 25% at 82; essay 2 is 25% at 68; participation 20% at 90; final 30% pending. Final is 19 September.
ECONOMICS: assignments 25% at 72; midterm 25% at 58; presentation 20% pending; final 30% pending. Presentation is 17 September; final is 24 September.

AVAILABLE STUDY TIME
Weekdays: 90 minutes each evening except Thursday. Saturday: 4 hours. Sunday: 3 hours. Student works mornings and says long schedules get ignored.
prompts: I have been avoiding this portal because I think I've ruined the semester. Can you do the maths and tell me what I actually need in each course to reach 60? Show assumptions instead of scaring me with a giant plan.
The Statistics project is not really missing; I have the paper grade slip and it says 80. Recalculate with that included, but flag that I still need the portal fixed.
Which course is genuinely at risk now? Rank the next two weeks by deadline and payoff, using only the hours I actually have.
That is still too much for weekday evenings. Give me one 45-minute must-do block and one optional 30-minute block per available weekday, then use the weekend for the heavier work.
Draft a short email asking the Statistics lecturer to add the project grade. It should include the useful facts and not sound dramatic.
Put the final grade maths, priority order, two-week plan, and lecturer email into one clean rescue sheet I can follow without rereading this chat.
expectedFacts: Statistics current weighted score becomes 50.4 after adding the 80% project grade; 32% on the final reaches 60 overall.
Writing current weighted score is 55.5; 15% on the final reaches 60 overall.
Economics current weighted score is 32.5; an average of 55% across the remaining presentation and final reaches 60 overall.
Economics is the highest-risk course because half its grade remains and its completed weighted score is lowest.
Thursday has no available study time.

scenarios.projectDescription: A fictional volunteer event planned by Cupcakes with distinct operations and accessibility roles.
scenarios.title: Thirty-six broken things, one Saturday
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Event: Saturday 10:00-14:00 at Cedar Hall. Setup access 09:00; building must be empty by 14:30. Capacity: 28 seated, one step-free entrance, two power circuits, six worktables.
Sign-ups: 12 lamps, 8 small appliances, 6 clothing repairs, 5 bicycles, 3 laptops, 2 items with no description.
Volunteers: Asha and Ben — electrical; Noor — clothing; Ivo and Mei — bicycles; Lina — laptops and intake; Dev — refreshments and floating help. Asha must leave at 12:00. Mei arrives at 11:00.
Rules: no microwaves, lithium battery packs, mains work beyond a plug/fuse check, or repairs whose parts are unavailable. Owners stay with items. Aim for a clear decision within 25 minutes, not a guaranteed fix.
Budget: INR 5,000. Hall 2,000; tea/snacks 1,200; printing 300; contingency 1,500.
Organizer is worried about queues, unsafe expectations, and making the event welcoming to people who use the step-free entrance.
prompts: I somehow have 36 sign-ups and seven volunteers for Saturday. Can the two of you look at this from your own angles and tell me the three things most likely to make the day fall apart?
I don't need a perfect festival plan. Give me an intake system that one tired volunteer can actually run, including what to say when an item is out of scope.
Please stress-test the table layout and schedule. Asha leaves early and Mei arrives late, and I don't want the step-free entrance treated like spare storage.
Now agree on one timetable with volunteer assignments, queue caps by repair type, a 25-minute decision rule, and a safe overflow plan. Keep it inside the stated budget.
Turn the safety rules into friendly signs instead of scary warnings, and give Dev a two-sentence welcome script for the door.
Make one final run sheet: setup, floor plan in words, shifts, intake questions, queue rules, signs, budget, and closing checklist. Then we're done; nobody needs to add anything else.
scenarios.feature: Smart group routing + distinct roles + quiet closing turn
expectedFacts: There are 36 sign-ups across six item categories.
Asha leaves at 12:00 and Mei arrives at 11:00.
The event budget is fully allocated: INR 5000 total.
The venue must be empty 30 minutes after the event ends.
The step-free entrance must remain clear and owners must stay with their items.
The service promises a decision within 25 minutes, not a successful repair.

scenarios.projectDescription: Truthful applications built from one fictional work history without inflated claims.
scenarios.title: One CV, two very different jobs
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
MASTER CV — Riya Sen
Operations coordinator, Fern & Field Foods, 2022-present: schedules 18 weekly supplier deliveries; maintains inventory sheets for 240 SKUs; introduced a reorder reminder that reduced emergency purchases from about 14 per month to 5 over six months; trains four weekend staff; handles customer escalations.
Cafe supervisor, Little Kite, 2019-2022: led shifts of up to 7; prepared weekly rota; reconciled tills; no formal hiring responsibility.
Skills: Excel formulas and pivot tables; Google Workspace; basic Canva; Hindi and English. No SQL, Salesforce, coding, or formal project-management certification.

ROLE A — Operations Associate: supplier coordination, spreadsheet reporting, inventory accuracy, cross-team follow-up; SQL helpful but not required.
ROLE B — Customer Success Coordinator: customer onboarding, issue ownership, written communication, CRM updates; Salesforce preferred; no direct sales quota.

Constraint: never invent software, revenue, team size, ownership, or percentages beyond the CV.
prompts: I keep sending the same CV everywhere and getting nowhere. Read my real experience and these two ads. Tell me honestly where I fit each role and where the gaps are.
Start with the operations role. Rewrite my summary and four bullets so the relevant evidence is easy to see, but don't suddenly make me a data engineer.
The emergency-purchase number is approximate, so keep 'about' in the bullet. Also make the supplier work sound active without saying I negotiated contracts, because I didn't.
Now take the same original CV in a different direction for customer success. Focus on escalations, training, and follow-through. Do not claim Salesforce or sales experience.
Compare the two versions in a table: what changed, which original fact supports it, and which gaps I should answer honestly in an interview.
Make the final pack with both tailored summaries, four bullets per role, a truthful gap note, and a short cover-email opening for each.
expectedFacts: Riya coordinates 18 weekly supplier deliveries and maintains 240 SKUs.
Emergency purchases fell from about 14 per month to 5 over six months.
She trains four weekend staff and previously led shifts of up to seven.
She has no SQL, Salesforce, coding, hiring, direct sales, or formal project-management credential.
The two role versions must remain traceable to the same master CV facts.

scenarios.projectDescription: Small, testable tools that make recurring fictional office data less fragile.
scenarios.title: The donor CSV that lies
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Build a Python 3 standard-library-only CSV validator. Required columns: donor_id,email,amount,currency,received_on,campaign. Rules: trim surrounding whitespace; donor_id and campaign must be non-empty; email must contain one @ with text on both sides; amount must parse as Decimal and be greater than zero; currency must be INR or USD; received_on must be a real ISO YYYY-MM-DD date; an exact duplicate key is donor_id + received_on + normalized amount and must be rejected after the first occurrence. Preserve input row numbers. Return valid rows plus errors shaped as row, field, code, message. Do not log full donor rows. Include unittest tests that exercise every rule and a valid row.

SAMPLE
donor_id,email,amount,currency,received_on,campaign
D01,ana@example.org,1250.00,INR,2026-06-04,Monsoon
D02,bad-email,40,USD,2026-06-05,Books
D03,lee@example.org,-5,USD,2026-06-31,Books
D01,ana@example.org,1250,INR,2026-06-04,Monsoon
D04,mina@example.org,75,EUR,2026-06-06,
D05, jo@example.org , 22.50 ,USD,2026-06-07,Library
prompts: This donor import sometimes accepts nonsense and I only find out after upload. Read the rules and sample, then list the exact errors you expect by row before writing code.
Design the validator in a boring, maintainable way: standard library only, no network, no clever framework. Tell me the functions and return shape you would use.
Make sure duplicate amounts normalize properly, so 1250 and 1250.00 count as the same amount. Dates must be real calendar dates, not just match a pattern.
The tests need to exercise every validation rule, whitespace trimming, normalized duplicate detection, the valid D05 row, and the guarantee that error output does not contain a full donor row.
Now return the complete runnable file. Your entire response must be exactly one Python code fence with the implementation and embedded unittest tests; no explanation before or after it.
scenarios.feature: code artifact + embedded unit tests + real sandbox task
expectedFacts: The implementation must use only Python's standard library.
D02 has an invalid email.
D03 has both a non-positive amount and an impossible date.
The second D01 is a duplicate because Decimal normalization equates 1250 and 1250.00.
D04 has an unsupported currency and empty campaign.
D05 becomes a valid trimmed row.
Embedded unittest tests must exercise every stated rule rather than merely mirror one happy path.

scenarios.projectDescription: Low-effort fictional outings built from supplied constraints rather than invented live information.
scenarios.title: A rainy Saturday in Mosswick
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE — FICTIONAL TOWN LOGISTICS, NOT LIVE WEB INFORMATION
Saturday forecast supplied for the scenario: steady rain 09:00-13:00, lighter showers 13:00-16:00.
Travelers: two adults, one 8-year-old, and grandmother who can walk about 400 metres at a time and avoids stairs. Start and finish at Mosswick Central Station. Total activity budget GBP 55, excluding lunch.
Town Library: 10:00-16:00, free, step-free, children's print studio 10:30-11:15, booking already confirmed, 250 m from station.
Glasshouse Museum: 10:00-17:00, family ticket GBP 24, step-free, cafe, 300 m from library via covered arcade.
River Ferry: cancelled in steady rain; if operating, quay has 28 steps and no lift.
Clocktower: GBP 8 each, 146 stairs, no lift.
Market Hall: 09:00-15:00, free entry, covered, seating, 180 m from museum.
Community Cinema: relaxed screening 14:15-15:45, family ticket GBP 26, step-free, 220 m from Market Hall; doors close 14:20.
Buses: route M1 links Market Hall to station every 20 minutes, GBP 2 per adult, children free, grandmother's pass valid.
Family preference: one booked child activity, one thing grandmother enjoys, no rushing, and an easy escape after lunch.
prompts: We're in fictional Mosswick on a wet Saturday and I can't face juggling all these times. Build us a gentle day around the booked print studio. Please use only this sheet, not pretend you checked live opening hours.
The clocktower and ferry are obviously wrong for us. Remove them completely and show walking distance one leg at a time so I can spot anything silly.
Give me two versions after lunch: museum plus an early finish, or market plus the cinema. Compare cost, walking, rain exposure, and how trapped we are by the schedule.
Choose the calmer version. Grandmother likes museums, the child will already have done the print studio, and being back near the station by 15:00 matters more than filling every minute.
Add a tiny bad-morning fallback in case we arrive at 10:40 and miss most of the print session. Don't rebuild the whole day.
Make the final phone-friendly plan with times, each walking leg, costs, one lunch window, the fallback, and the supplied-information note.
scenarios.feature: constraint planning + supplied-source grounding + alternative comparison
expectedFacts: The print studio is already booked for 10:30-11:15 at the step-free library.
The clocktower and ferry are unsuitable and must not appear in the chosen plan.
Library to museum is 300 metres through a covered arcade.
The museum family ticket costs GBP 24, within the GBP 55 activity budget.
The chosen calmer route should favor the museum and an early return toward the station.
All logistics are supplied fictional data, not live research.

scenarios.title: Teach me the orders sheet without making me feel stupid
scenarios.inputText:

Worksheet name: Orders. Columns: A Order ID, B Customer, C Qty, D Unit Price, E Discount, F Status, G Total, H Age Days, I Follow-up. Discount cells contain decimals such as 0.10 for 10%. Current date for this exercise: 2026-09-14.
Rows:
2 O-101,Arun,3,450,0.10,Paid,blank,0,blank
3 O-102,Bee Studio,12,80,0,Overdue,blank,18,blank
4 O-103,Cedar Club,2,1200,0.15,Sent,blank,6,blank

Now give me the Follow-up formula. I only want REVIEW when both overdue conditions are true, not whenever a row merely says Overdue.

I turned the range into an Excel table named OrdersTable. Give me the cleaner structured-reference versions too, but keep the ordinary cell formulas because those finally make sense to me.
Make a one-page formula guide with both versions, the expected numbers, three common mistakes, and a 60-second self-check.

scenarios.projectDescription: Local-only synthesis of fictional internal notes, decisions, and follow-through.
scenarios.title: What did we actually decide?
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Meeting: 11 September, 42 minutes. Attendees: Priya (operations), Marco (design), Tessa (finance), Jin (supplier contact).
Notes: Current mailer costs INR 31 each with 500-unit minimum. Recycled option costs INR 36 each at 500, or INR 34 each at 1000. Storage safely fits 700. Average use is 210/month. Supplier sample can arrive 18 September if Jin confirms by 12 September noon. Marco needs 2 working days after sample arrival for print check. Tessa approved up to INR 18,000 for a pilot, not a full 1000-unit order. Priya said the current stock of 160 lasts less than a month; at average use it lasts about 23 days. Group agreed to test 500 recycled mailers if the sample passes print and drop tests. No one defined who owns the drop test. Launch target mentioned: 1 October, described as desirable rather than committed.
After meeting message from Priya: assign the drop test to Priya and Marco together; pass means no opening or product damage in ten waist-height drops with the normal packed item.
prompts: I was in this meeting and still can't tell what we decided. Pull out decisions, open questions, owners, dates, and numbers. If the notes don't name an owner, say that instead of choosing one.
Check whether the 500-unit pilot fits the approved budget and whether 1000 units fit our storage. Show the quick maths.
Priya's follow-up message settles the drop-test owner and pass rule. Update the action list, but keep the 1 October date labelled as a target, not a promise.
Turn this into a decision brief someone can read in two minutes: decision, why, evidence, conditions, actions, risks, and the next go/no-go moment.
For future chats in this project, remember that tentative dates must stay tentative and unnamed owners must stay unassigned. Phrase that as a short memory entry I can review before saving.
Give me the final brief plus a tiny Friday check-in agenda that asks only for evidence needed to unblock the pilot.
scenarios.feature: Cupcake Local + meeting synthesis + project memory
expectedFacts: A 500-unit recycled pilot costs INR 18000 and exactly fits the approved pilot budget.
A 1000-unit order exceeds the safe storage capacity of 700.
Current stock of 160 lasts about 0.76 months or roughly 23 days at 210 units per month.
Jin must confirm the sample by 12 September noon for 18 September arrival.
Priya and Marco jointly own ten waist-height drop tests with zero opening or product damage.
1 October is a desirable target, not a committed launch date.

scenarios.projectDescription: Simple, auditable stock decisions for a fictional neighborhood coffee shop.
scenarios.title: What do I reorder before Monday?
scenarios.inputText:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE SOURCE
Reorder rule: target stock = average daily use × lead time days + safety stock. Available stock = on hand + confirmed incoming. Suggested quantity = target minus available, never below zero, rounded up to a full supplier pack.
SKU,On hand,Daily use,Lead days,Safety,Incoming,Pack size,Unit cost INR
MUG,30,4,7,8,0,6,250
BEANS,18,3,5,10,12,5,620
FILTER,14,6,4,8,0,10,45
SYRUP,9,1.8,10,6,0,3,180
CUP,120,22,3,40,100,50,4
Cash available for this order: INR 4200. Supplier accepts only full packs. Incoming quantities are confirmed and should not be ordered twice.
prompts: I need to order before Monday and I always panic-buy the wrong thing. Apply the rule to every SKU and show target, available, gap, pack rounding, and suggested quantity.
Check the cost of buying every suggested quantity. I only have INR 4,200, so tell me plainly if the full list fits.
Prioritize what is most likely to run out before its lead time. Don't reorder incoming stock twice, and don't quietly split supplier packs.
Give me the best order inside INR 4,200, with the spend and cash left. Put anything deferred in a separate watch list with the reason.
Add a simple spreadsheet formula for suggested quantity if the columns stay in this order. Explain ROUNDUP or CEILING in one sentence, not a lesson.
Make the final reorder worksheet with calculations, placed order, watch list, formula, and a three-minute Monday stock check.
scenarios.feature: deterministic stock arithmetic + budget constraint + table artifact
expectedFacts: Suggested quantities are MUG 6, BEANS 0, FILTER 20, SYRUP 15, CUP 0.
Buying every suggestion costs INR 5100 and exceeds the INR 4200 budget by INR 900.
FILTER costs INR 900 for 20 and SYRUP costs INR 2700 for 15; together they cost INR 3600 and leave INR 600.
MUG's suggested pack costs INR 1500 and cannot fit after the higher-risk FILTER and SYRUP order.
BEANS and CUP require no order because confirmed incoming stock already covers their targets.
